description: Dashed squares mark positions before an operation and do not count toward the current deque. A solid square outside the container shows the value returned by the removal. Arrows at both ends of the first panel show the directions of insertion and removal.

steps.announcement: The front example starts independently with [3, 2, 5, 4]. The next operation acts on the front.
steps.explanation: The front example starts afresh with four elements, [3, 2, 5, 4], with 3 at the front and 4 at the rear. There is no return value. This starting state still contains 4, so it does not continue from the removal of 4 in the other example.
steps.key_state: The deque is [3, 2, 5, 4], with 3 at the front and 4 at the rear. There is no return value.
steps.title: Independent starting state

steps.announcement: Adding 1 at the front gives the deque [1, 3, 2, 5, 4].
steps.explanation: The call push_first(1) adds 1 at the front. The other elements keep their order. The deque now contains five elements, [1, 3, 2, 5, 4], with 1 at the front and 4 at the rear. The call returns no value.
steps.key_state: The deque is [1, 3, 2, 5, 4], with 1 at the front and 4 at the rear. There is no return value.
steps.title: push_first(1)

steps.announcement: Removing and returning 1 from the front restores the deque to [3, 2, 5, 4].
steps.explanation: The call pop_first() removes and returns 1 from the front. The deque is back to four elements, [3, 2, 5, 4], with 3 at the front and 4 at the rear. The returned 1 is outside the deque.
steps.key_state: The deque is [3, 2, 5, 4], with 3 at the front and 4 at the rear. The call returns 1.
steps.title: pop_first()

prose.summary: Add an element at the front and then remove that same element. The others keep their order.
prose.title: Operations at the front of a deque

description: Dashed squares mark positions before an operation and do not count toward the current deque. A solid square outside the container shows the value returned by the removal. Arrows at both ends of the first panel show the directions of insertion and removal.

steps.announcement: The rear example starts with [3, 2, 5]. The next operation acts on the rear.
steps.explanation: The rear example starts with three elements, [3, 2, 5]. The front is 3 and the rear is 5. There is no return value.
steps.key_state: The deque is [3, 2, 5], with 3 at the front and 5 at the rear. There is no return value.
steps.title: Independent starting state

steps.announcement: Adding 4 at the rear gives the deque [3, 2, 5, 4].
steps.explanation: The call push_last(4) adds 4 at the rear. The other elements keep their order. The deque now contains four elements, [3, 2, 5, 4], with 3 at the front and 4 at the rear. The call returns no value.
steps.key_state: The deque is [3, 2, 5, 4], with 3 at the front and 4 at the rear. There is no return value.
steps.title: push_last(4)

steps.announcement: Removing and returning 4 from the rear restores the deque to [3, 2, 5].
steps.explanation: The call pop_last() removes and returns 4 from the rear. The deque is back to three elements, [3, 2, 5], with 3 at the front and 5 at the rear. The returned 4 is outside the deque.
steps.key_state: The deque is [3, 2, 5], with 3 at the front and 5 at the rear. The call returns 4.
steps.title: pop_last()

prose.summary: Add an element at the rear and then remove that same element. The others keep their order.

context: Five vertical panels run from left to right. The top is the front and the bottom is the rear. All sequences in the table below run from front to rear. The first three panels show the initial state, insertion at the rear, and removal from the rear. The last two show insertion at the front and removal from the front.

Although arrows point right between panels, the panel showing insertion at the front still contains 4. It cannot follow directly from the previous panel, where 4 was removed. The front example starts separately with [3, 2, 5, 4]. This starting state has no panel of its own. The table includes it, which gives six rows in all.
description: Dashed squares mark positions before an operation and do not count toward the current deque. A solid square outside the container shows the value returned by the removal. Arrows at both ends of the first panel show the directions of insertion and removal.

frames.explanation: The rear example adds and then removes 4 at the rear. The front example adds and then removes 1 at the front. In both cases, the other elements keep their relative order. A deque supports insertion and removal at both ends.
frames.title: Operations at the front and rear of a deque

summary: Two examples show the four basic deque operations: insertion and removal at the rear, then insertion and removal at the front.
